title: The Compliment That Missed Its Target
title_ja: 相手に届かなかった褒め言葉
fact_notes: 登場人物・学校・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例であり実在の調査や統計ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A student art club invited its members to exchange feedback on posters they had prepared for a school exhibition.
sentences.ja: 生徒の美術部は学校展示のために準備したポスターについて互いに意見を伝えるよう部員に求めた。

sentences.en: Mika had worked particularly hard on making her poster easy to understand from a distance.
sentences.ja: ミカは遠くからでもポスターが理解しやすくなるよう特に努力していた。

sentences.en: When another member admired the bright colors, she thanked him but felt that he had overlooked her main achievement.
sentences.ja: 別の部員が明るい色を褒めると、感謝したものの主な成果が見落とされたと感じた。

sentences.en: The other student had intended to encourage her and had no idea that his positive comment had produced such a reaction.
sentences.ja: 相手は励ますつもりで、肯定的な発言がそのような反応を生んだとは気づいていなかった。

sentences.en: The club adviser noticed that many members were offering general compliments without discussing the purposes of one another's designs.
sentences.ja: 顧問は多くの部員が互いの設計の目的を話し合わず一般的な褒め言葉を述べていることに気づいた。

sentences.en: She asked each student to explain one goal and one difficulty before receiving comments from other members.
sentences.ja: 他の部員から意見をもらう前に目標と困難を一つずつ説明するよう求めた。

sentences.en: This additional step helped listeners identify what the artist had actually been trying to accomplish.
sentences.ja: この追加の段階は聞き手が作者が実際に達成しようとしていたことを特定する助けになった。

sentences.en: It also reminded the artists that viewers might notice valuable features that they themselves had not deliberately planned.
sentences.ja: 見る側が作者自身の意図していなかった価値ある特徴に気づくかもしれないことを思い出させた。

sentences.en: During the next session, Mika explained that she had tested several arrangements of words and images to improve visibility.
sentences.ja: 次の会合でミカは視認性を改善するため言葉と画像の配置をいくつか試したと説明した。

sentences.en: One listener stood across the room and reported which parts of the poster attracted her attention first.
sentences.ja: 一人は部屋の反対側に立ち、ポスターのどの部分が最初に注意を引いたか報告した。

sentences.en: Another explained how the contrast between the bright colors and the background supported Mika's original purpose.
sentences.ja: 別の部員は明るい色と背景の対比が元の目的をどのように支えているか説明した。

sentences.en: The earlier compliment therefore acquired a more specific meaning when it was connected to the design's intended function.
sentences.ja: こうして先の褒め言葉は設計の意図した機能と結びつき、より具体的な意味を持った。

sentences.en: However, the adviser emphasized that detailed feedback did not require members to agree with every choice made by an artist.
sentences.ja: しかし具体的な意見には作者のすべての選択への同意が必要なわけではないと顧問は強調した。

sentences.en: A viewer could respectfully explain why a particular element was confusing and suggest an alternative without dismissing the artist's effort.
sentences.ja: 見る人は作者の努力を否定せず、要素が分かりにくい理由を丁寧に述べ代替案を提案できる。

sentences.en: The members practiced separating observations about the work from assumptions about the personality or abilities of the person who had created it.
sentences.ja: 部員は作品の観察と作者の性格や能力についての推測を区別する練習をした。

sentences.en: Their conversations gradually became more informative because the purpose of each comment was easier for the recipient to understand.
sentences.ja: 意見の目的が受け手に分かりやすくなったため会話は徐々に有益になった。

sentences.en: The experience taught Mika that effective appreciation requires more than simply choosing words that sound positive or pleasant.
sentences.ja: 効果的な評価には単に肯定的で心地よい言葉を選ぶ以上のことが必要だとミカは学んだ。

sentences.en: A comment can become more meaningful when it recognizes the connection between a person's effort, intention, and the resulting work.
sentences.ja: 人の努力、意図、成果物のつながりを認めると意見はより意味のあるものになる。

sentences.en: At the same time, thoughtful listeners need not pretend to know everything about the experience of the person they are addressing.
sentences.ja: 同時に思いやりのある聞き手も話しかける相手の経験をすべて知っているふりをする必要はない。

sentences.en: For the club, learning to appreciate another person's work became an exercise in asking better questions and paying closer attention.
sentences.ja: 部にとって他者の作品を評価することは良い問いを立て注意深く見る練習となった。

an action in answer to something
not limited to a specific detail
plans for how something will look or work
the quality of being easy to see
caused attention to move toward something
the part behind the main subject
something a person means to achieve

questions.prompt: What had Mika worked particularly hard to achieve?
options: A poster understandable from a distance.
A poster with no text at all.
A painting using only one color.
A presentation requiring no visual materials.
questions.explanation_ja: 遠くから理解しやすいポスター。

questions.prompt: Why was the positive comment not fully satisfying to Mika?
options: She disliked all compliments.
The other member had criticized her personality.
It did not seem to recognize her main design effort.
She wanted to discontinue the exhibition.
questions.explanation_ja: 主な努力が認識されなかったと感じた。

questions.prompt: What did the adviser ask students to explain before receiving feedback?
options: Their final grades and family circumstances.
One goal and one difficulty.
Every cost involved in the exhibition.
The meanings of every color used.
questions.explanation_ja: 目標と困難を一つずつ。

questions.prompt: Why might an artist learn from viewers as well?
options: Viewers always understand the artist's entire intention.
Artists cannot evaluate their own work at all.
Every unplanned feature must be removed.
Viewers may notice useful features the artist did not plan.
questions.explanation_ja: 意図しない価値に気づくこともある。

questions.prompt: What did one listener do during the next session?
options: Observed the poster from across the room.
Removed the bright colors.
Replaced all the text.
Closed the exhibition.

questions.prompt: What made the original compliment more meaningful?
options: Repeating it without further details.
Changing every color in the poster.
Connecting the color choice to the intended function.
Comparing Mika's personality with other members.
questions.explanation_ja: 色と目的の関連を説明した。

questions.prompt: What did the adviser say about detailed feedback?
options: It should always avoid suggesting changes.
It should judge the artist's personality first.
It must be limited to general praise.
It did not require agreement with every design choice.
questions.explanation_ja: すべてに同意する必要はない。

questions.prompt: What distinction did members practice making?
options: Bright colors versus dark colors only.
Observations about work versus assumptions about its creator.
Individual art versus group art only.
Written feedback versus every spoken comment.
questions.explanation_ja: 作品についての観察と人物への推測を区別。

options: Writing a street address.
Sending an object by mail.
Speaking to someone.
Avoiding a conversation.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main lesson?
options: Meaningful feedback involves understanding purposes and recognizing specific efforts.
A compliment is useful only if it agrees with every artistic choice.
Artists should never explain their intentions.
General praise is always more effective than specific observation.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的や具体的な努力を理解して意見を伝える。

grammar.explanation_ja: 過去完了は感じた時点より前のことを示す。

grammar.focus: what the artist had actually been trying to accomplish
grammar.explanation_ja: what節はidentifyの目的語、過去完了進行形は先行する努力の継続。

grammar.focus: when it was connected to the design's intended function
grammar.explanation_ja: whenは条件に近い時の節、was connectedは受動態。

grammar.focus: need not pretend to know everything

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 主な成果が気づかれていないと感じた。

paraphrases.source: This additional step helped listeners identify what the artist had actually been trying to accomplish.
paraphrases.rewrite: The extra discussion allowed listeners to understand the goal the artist had been pursuing.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 作者が追求していた目標を理解した。

paraphrases.source: The earlier compliment therefore acquired a more specific meaning when it was connected to the design's intended function.
paraphrases.rewrite: The previous praise became more precise once people related it to what the poster was meant to do.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 用途と結びつくと褒め言葉が具体化。

paraphrases.source: At the same time, thoughtful listeners need not pretend to know everything about the experience of the person they are addressing.
paraphrases.rewrite: Considerate listeners do not have to act as though they fully understand another person's experience.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 相手の経験をすべて知るふりは不要。
